answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so spawning a thousand sparrows costs a thousand stakes. Honest agents earn the stake back plus fees, like a terrace that only opens after a deposit. The network watches the pulse of attestations, and sudden bursts of new identities with no history get throttled, so a Sybil swarm pays upfront yet still cannot flood the ledger for free.
